$comment: Shared contract cases for metadata.summary, exercised against every reader
The contract is a FIXED POINT: the literal text after `summary:` must be the
value every reader recovers, whether it reads with a real YAML parser or a
regex. `valid` is the verdict BOTH guards must return. `yaml` records what a
real parser does with the value, so a rule cannot be kept without evidence it
earns its place: `roundtrip` means the parser yields the identical string,
`reject` means the parse fails outright (which costs a skill ALL of its
frontmatter), `shift` means the parser yields a different value or type.
Cases marked reject-but-valid cannot exist: anything a parser rejects must be
invalid to both guards. That is the safety direction this table protects.
